To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the benefits of phosphorus ( P ) stewardship for society are not well recognized due to the focus of research on the impacts of P on water quality and agriculture, 2) P stewardship can have positive co‐benefits for ecosystem services, such that the management of P for one purpose can have positive impacts on multiple ecosystem processes and functions, 3) there is an opportunity to align P stewardhip with the management of ecosystem services, 4) the key research priorities
the benefits of sustainable phosphorus use and management for ecosystem services are rarely recognized.
the benefits of sustainable phosphorus management extend to multiple ecosystem services, and that the impacts of phosphorus on ecosystem services are context‐dependent.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the management of phosphorus (a critical element in the global food system) can impact multiple ecosystem services.
understanding and communicating how P stewardship can be used to optimize multiple ecosystem services.
the role of phosphorus in supporting multiple ecosystem services and how phosphorus stewardship can be optimized to support the provision of multiple ecosystem services.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
phosphorus (P)-based stewardship can provide co-benefits for multiple ecosystem services and should be considered a priority for agricultural policy and management.
the P‐ecosystem service cascade is a powerful tool to guide P stewardship for the multiple ecosystem services that underpin human well‐being.
P stewardship is a necessary component of managing multiple ecosystem services, and that the framework proposed here is a useful tool to guide future research in this area.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the phosphorus cascade framework is a powerful tool for guiding phosphorus stewardship to optimize for ecosystem service co‐ benefits.
phosphorus is essential for life, and its use and management have important implications for multiple ecosystem services, but the full extent of these impacts is rarely acknowledged.
P stewardship is an important component of sustainable agriculture and that P stewardship can provide multiple co‐benefits for the environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that

phosphorus stewardship can be a powerful lever to simultaneously improve agricultural productivity and the provision of multiple ecosystem services in the face of a growing human population and climate change.
P stewardship can be a key tool for managing multiple ecosystem services and for achieving multiple goals of sustainable development.
P stewardship can be a win–win for both agriculture and the environment, but only if it is designed to account for multiple ecosystem services.
